kaartje
Walnut phonograph · Delft
press me
№ 01Kaartje

A voice you can post.

A small walnut phonograph. Speak into it, seal your voice into a paper card, and send the card by mail. Whoever receives it holds it to their own Kaartje — and hears you.

Scroll to follow one card from your desk to theirs.

№ 02Record

Hold the knob. Say it.

Hold a blank card against the back. The screen asks you to speak. Hold the brass knob and talk — up to sixty seconds, with a timer and a live waveform.

Recording only happens here, on the machine. Every card carries a voice that was really spoken into it.

№ 03Seal

Let go. It's sealed.

Release the knob and the recording is bound to that one card. The screen reads Sealed. Ready to send. Not happy? Hold again and re-record before you post it.

Inside each card: a paper-thin NFC tag holding only a long random link. The voice itself never lives on the paper.

№ 04Write & post

Then write on it, like a postcard.

Cotton paper, 350 g — fountain pens welcome. A few lines on the back, an envelope, a stamp.

“Lieve oma, listen to this one before bed.”

№ 05Receive

Touch it to the back. Hear them.

No app, no login. The receiver touches the card to the back of their Kaartje; the screen shows who it's from and the voice plays.

Grandparents don't need to learn anything new. Hold the card to it. That's all.

№ 06Machine to machine

Two machines, one goodnight.

  1. Pair two Kaartjes once, with a QR code.
  2. No card on the back? Hold the knob, speak, let go — it's sent.
  3. On their side, your name slowly breathes on the screen. One press plays it.
  4. When they've listened, a small heart appears on yours.
№ 07Made to keep

One block of walnut. No screws.

The body is milled from a single block of North American black walnut, oiled twice and never lacquered. The grille is cut straight through the wood.

All electronics ride on one printed frame that slides in from the back. The back cover holds on four magnets; the battery unplugs, so you can replace it yourself.

Brass knob, brushed and unplated — it darkens with your hand. Grey wool felt underneath.

№ 08One control

Everything is the knob.

PressPlay / pause
HoldRecord — release to finish
TurnVolume; in standby, scroll back through past voices
Hold 5 sWi-Fi setup — a QR code appears

Try it: click the brass knob on the model.

№ 09Quiet by default

The screen is dark until it matters.

A warm amber OLED sits behind tinted acrylic, set into the wood. Off, you can't see its edge. On, the words seem to float up out of the walnut.

No clock, no icons, nothing left lit. It wakes for a voice and goes back to sleep thirty seconds later.
